======================================================================================
reading
======================================================================================

A process that is blocked -- on a message pump, a crash dialog, a file
handle -- accrues no CPU while it waits. These accrue it continuously at
close to one core for as long as they are allowed to run, and produce no
output. That is a spin inside the compiler, not a crash and not a prompt
waiting for someone to click it.

The trivial control matters: it shows the release is not simply unusable
in this harness. Same binary, same working directory, same command shape.

So these two releases do not exhibit the signature the issue reports.
They fail earlier and differently. match-crash.json exists to keep that
distinction visible in the release scan, where the primary predicate
scores both as reproductions via timed_out.

What this does NOT establish: that the spin is unbounded. It was not
allowed to run past 240s. The honest statement is 'did not terminate
within 240s while burning CPU throughout', not 'infinite loop'.
